claims.text: Asked how an unreported program is funded: 'misappropriation of funds and self-fund.' Asked whether corporations overcharge government and divert the excess: 'Correct, through something called IR&D.'

Sworn testimony, 26 July 2023: 'I was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-ons when I requested it. I made the decision based on the data I collected to report this information to my superiors and multiple inspectors general and, in effect, becoming a whistleblower. As you know, I have suffered retaliation for my decision'.

Sworn testimony, 26 July 2023, on recovered biological material: asked by Rep. Mace whether the biologics recovered were 'human or nonhuman', Grusch answered 'Nonhuman, and that was the assessment of people with direct knowledge on the program I talked to that are currently still on the program.'

Under oath he gave the chain by which the case reached investigators and then the public: 'It was not until 2009, until Jay Stratton had contacted me to investigate. Unbeknownst to all, he was part of the ATIP program in the Pentagon led by Lue Elizondo. There was an unofficial official report that came out that is now on the internet. Years later, I was contacted by the other pilot, Alex Dietrich, and asked if I would been contacted and I said no, but I am willing to talk. I was contacted by Mr. Elizondo, and we talked for a short period of time.' This is the provenance chain in the words of the witness, under oath.

Under oath he gave the reason the aircrew were airborne at all: 'We were at a work up with all the battle groups. So, we integrate the ships with the carrier, the airwing with the carrier, and we start working. So, we were doing an air to air defense to hone not only our skills but those of the USS Princeton when they had been tracking them for 2 weeks. The problem was that there was never manned aircraft airborne when they were tracking them and this was the first day and, unfortunately, we were the ones airborne and went and saw it.'

Under oath he gave the radar picture of the 14 November 2004 intercept, in answer to Rep. Langworthy: 'The Princeton tracked it. The Nimitz tracked it. The E2 tracked it. We never saw it on our radars. Our fire control radars never picked it up. The other airplane that took the video did get it on a radar. As soon as it tried to lock it, it jammed the radar, spit the lock and he rapidly switched over to the targeting pod, which you can do in the F-18.'

Asked by Rep. Langworthy 'is it true that you saw, in your words, a 40-foot flying Tic Tac shaped object?', he answered under oath: 'That is correct. For some people that cannot--know what a Tic Tac is it is a giant flying propane tank.'

Witness of record at the 26 July 2023 House Oversight hearing: 'Commander David Fravor (Ret.), Former Commanding Officer, United States Navy'. Written statement, Truth in Testimony form and bio filed in the House Committee Repository, event 116282.

The testimony was sworn, and the printed record carries the mechanism. Chairman Grothman: 'Pursuant to Committee Rule 9(g), the witnesses will please stand and raise their right hands. Let the record show that all the witnesses answered in the affirmative.'

And there were many great reasons, but one of them was actually--had to do with UAPs.' He tied it forward to the NASA independent study team and to Harvard standing up the Galileo Project in 2021.

edges.note: Frost asked Graves two questions: 'can you discuss the importance of seeking scientists to sit on your advisory board?' and 'how might Congress help to facilitate partnerships between the scientific community and the UAP focus groups within government?' Graves answered that this 'is going to be a scientific problem, and not only that, it is also an engineering problem', and pointed to his work with the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics to stand up a UAP integration committee.
